name: Stream Data Centers

profile.campus: Stream Dallas-Fort Worth area (DFWA site, Garland, TX, not the same campus as the separate DFW IV site)
profile.reading: Stream Data Centers DFWA sits at 1813 Lookout Drive in Garland, Texas, one of Stream Dallas-Fort Worth area facilities. Per Stream own site, the 23-acre site carries 43 megawatts of critical capacity across 275,000 square feet, served by a dedicated 95 megawatt Oncor electric substation. Phase 1 was commissioned in January 2020, and the facility was reported fully leased as of 2023 to an unnamed major cloud customer. Stream own Dallas facilities page states no shared-campus relationship between DFWA and the separate DFW IV facility elsewhere in the metro area, which sits in Richardson and was sold by Stream back in 2011, well before DFWA was commissioned, so the two should be understood as unrelated Stream projects in the same broad market rather than phases of one campus. Stream Data Centers was founded in 1999 in Dallas, Texas, originally as a technical real estate affiliate of Stream Realty Partners, a larger commercial real estate firm. Ownership has changed more recently: Apollo-managed funds announced acquisition of a majority stake in Stream in August 2025 and completed the deal in November 2025, with Principal Asset Management taking a minority stake and Stream management retaining a minority position, and Stream now describes itself as a key operating platform within the Apollo ecosystem. The company markets its wholesale, powered-shell, and build-to-suit data center model, claiming more than 90 percent of its capacity leased to Fortune 100 customers and describing a pipeline exceeding four gigawatts with more than 27 delivered developments across markets including Dallas-Fort Worth, Phoenix, Chicago, San Antonio, and Atlanta. Garland sits in the eastern Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex, a submarket that has drawn substantial hyperscale investment in recent years thanks to available land, strong Oncor grid capacity, and proximity to the broader Dallas fiber and interconnection ecosystem centered around older facilities like the Infomart, factors consistent with Stream decision to secure a dedicated 95 megawatt substation for this specific site.
profile.research_note: 43 MW / 275,000 sqft / 23-acre site / 95MW Oncor substation / Jan 2020 Phase 1 commissioning sourced to Stream own Dallas facilities page. Explicitly noted DFWA and DFW IV are not the same campus, since both are in this operator dataset and could otherwise be confused. Company background from Stream own history/news pages.

profile.duplicate_rationale: Stream Data Centers is the same company as the already profiled Stream operator record (uid dca83e71). Stream Data Centers, headquartered in Dallas, Texas, is a colocation and build to suit data center developer owned by Ridgemont Equity Partners as of 2024. This record is a duplicate entry for the same company and is linked rather than merged.

reading:
This row duplicates the Stream operator record already held in this registry at uid dca83e71, and it is retained and cross linked rather than deleted, consistent with registry policy against removing rows. Stream Data Centers is a Dallas based developer and operator of build to suit and wholesale colocation space, active since the 1990s and owned by Ridgemont Equity Partners. What this row carries that is worth reading is one specific building, and the public record for it is good enough to be worth setting out.

The Texas facility here is DFWA, Stream's Garland site at 1813 Lookout Drive in Garland, Texas. Stream publishes it as 275,000 square feet at 43 megawatts, fully leased, taking two feeds from an on site Oncor substation rated at 95 megawatts. Those three numbers describe three different things and are easy to run together. The 95 megawatts is the capacity of the substation sitting on the property, the 43 megawatts is what Stream markets the building as supporting, and neither is a statement of what the tenant currently draws. Stream does not publish a separate critical IT load figure for the building, so the 43 megawatt number should be read as the site's marketed capacity rather than as measured IT load.

The construction record adds a phase history that the marketing page flattens. The electrical contractor on the project describes a 23 acre site in Garland with an expandable single building of 138,132 square feet and 40 megawatts of utility feeds from an on site substation, completed in 2019 with J.E. Dunn as general contractor. Read together with Stream's current 275,000 square foot listing, those are almost certainly successive phases of the same expandable site rather than contradictory figures, and this entry treats them that way rather than picking one and discarding the other.

The Garland building is small relative to what Stream now builds in the same metropolitan area, and the comparison is the useful context. Stream's DFWB campus in Wilmer, in south Dallas County, runs 690,000 square feet across three buildings at 90 megawatts and is fully leased, also on an on site Oncor substation. DFWC, sometimes called Wilmer II, is under construction as three buildings of about 508,000 square feet and 80 megawatts each, 240 megawatts across a campus of more than 1.52 million square feet, served by an on site Oncor substation rated up to 372 megawatts. The step from a 43 megawatt single building in 2019 to a 240 megawatt campus fed by a 372 megawatt substation is a compact illustration of how quickly the unit of development changed in this market.

Stream also lists four earlier Dallas facilities, its DFW I through VI series dating to the late 1990s, as sold or divested. That is a reminder that Stream's model has always included developing and exiting as well as holding, so a count of facilities it currently operates understates what it has built, and a building carrying the Stream name in an older directory may no longer be a Stream asset.
